definition: Predicting missing or future edges in a network — friend suggestions, citation links, KG completion.
details: Predicting missing or future edges in a network — friend suggestions, citation links, KG completion.

explainer.lead: Link prediction forecasts missing or future edges in a network. It matters for suggesting connections and completing knowledge graphs where links are absent or not yet observed.

tiers.eli5: Like guessing which two friends in a group will become friends next, based on who they already know and what they have in common.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers score candidate node pairs from graph structure or learned embeddings and rank them to propose edges. The pitfall is that a predicted link can be genuinely absent rather than merely unobserved, so evaluation must handle this ambiguity.
tiers.paperLevel: Link prediction is the task of predicting missing or future edges in a network, applied to cases such as friend suggestions, citation links, and knowledge graph completion. The definition does not prescribe a scoring method, so approaches range across structural and learned models.

explainer.example: A social platform scores pairs of users who share many mutual connections and proposes the highest-scoring pairs as friend suggestions.
